subject: Stratagem Health — KMS/HSM artifacts and rotation walkthrough
messages:
From: Jacob Morris <jacob.morris@stratagemhealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: security_ops@stratagemhealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 Jan 2028 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Evidence request: KMS/HSM controls and rotation history

Hi Aditya —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our SIG/SOC2 intake we're collecting a compact evidence bundle for encryption and key management. Could you help us with the following items (we’re trying to scope what we can attach to the questionnaire this week):

- A short description of Redwood's BYOK handshake for tenant-supplied keys (sequence diagram or bullets).
- HSM attestation or vendor-signed statement covering the 2027 Q4 snapshot.
- Key rotation log export for tenant KEKs and wrapping keys (last 12 months).
- Example KV/prefix cache retention policy and any snapshot retention notes for encrypted artifacts.
- Network/TLS cipher list in use for in-transit encryption endpoints, and whether mutual TLS is supported for private deployments.
- Proof of operator access controls for HSM (operator matrix / sample access logs).

If you can attach anything as a compact archive (or link to a drive folder), that would be ideal. Otherwise we can set a short call to walk through what you can share.

Target timeline: by end of next week (2028-01-17) if possible.

Thanks,
Jacob
Sr. Security Engineer
Stratagem Health
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Morris <jacob.morris@stratagemhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jan 2028 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evidence request: KMS/HSM controls and rotation history

Jacob —

Appreciate the clear list. We can provide a compact bundle that covers all of these items. High level plan:

- BYOK handshake: one-page sequence plus a short exported transcript of the enrollment API calls (sanitized).
- HSM attestation: vendor attestation PDF (2027-12-31) and a short explanation of how we bind attestation to tenant keys.
- Rotation logs: we’ll produce a filtered export (last 12 months) showing rotation events, operator id, and key IDs.
- Retention: policy excerpt + sample manifest showing prefix cache TTLs and retention for backups.
- TLS ciphers: current endpoints + notes on mTLS support for Private deployments.
- Operator access: redacted operator access matrix and an example of an HSM operator session log (audit stub).

Ben and Marissa are looping in the artifacts. I’ll schedule a 30-minute sync for Thursday (2028-01-13) to review the items and decide what goes into the SIG packet versus what should be handed over under an NDA.

Do you have a preferred link for upload or should we place the bundle in our shared Drive folder and grant Stratagem access?

—Aditya
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Morris <jacob.morris@stratagemhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Jan 2028 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evidence request: KMS/HSM controls and rotation history

Jacob / team —

Attaching a short artifacts index and a stubbed archive (see filenames below). A few implementation notes to help you map items to the SIG questionnaire:

1) BYOK workflow (redwood_byok_handshake_summary.pdf) — covers API flow, nonce exchange, and KEK wrapping. We sanitize tenant identifiers before delivery.

2) HSM attestation (hsm_attestation-2027-12-31.pdf) — vendor-signed attestation from our HSM provider; it references the hardware module serial ranges used in Q4. I’ve added a single-paragraph note about how we record attestation IDs in the tenant audit trail.

3) Rotation logs (rotation-log-sample-2027.tar.gz) — CSV export with event timestamps, key_id (hashed), rotation_type, and operator_id (redacted). If you need the full unredacted set we require an auditable transfer under our data transfer MOU.

4) Operator access (operator-matrix-sample.csv) — role -> operator mapping for HSM ops. We include a sample session log (audit stub) for one rotation event.

5) TLS and transport — short text block in the summary PDF; endpoints use TLS1.3 with a tiered cipher list. mTLS is supported on Redwood Private with customer-provided certs.

Upload preference: we created a shared Drive folder (link sent below) and granted view access to security_ops@stratagemhealth.com. If you need a signed NDA before we include operator-level logs, flag that and we’ll route it to Legal.

Attachment stubs: redwood_byok_handshake_summary.pdf (11 pages), hsm_attestation-2027-12-31.pdf (4 pages), rotation-log-sample-2027.tar.gz (1 archive, contains CSVs), operator-matrix-sample.csv

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jacob Morris <jacob.morris@stratagemhealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, security_ops@stratagemhealth.com
Date: Mon, 17 Jan 2028 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evidence request: KMS/HSM controls and rotation history

Thanks — this looks good. We were able to review the bundle in the Drive link and the summary maps cleanly to the SIG questions. A couple quick follow-ups:

- For the rotation logs, can you confirm timezone of timestamps (UTC vs PST) and whether the rotation_type field differentiates automatic vs manual rotations?
- For the BYOK transcript, can you include the API call sample that shows the key-wrapping response header (sanitized)? That helps our reviewers validate the wrapping step.
- For operator access, the reviewer asked for one sample audit record with the operator id hashed but the action details intact — the redacted example you provided is close, but they want one complete audit row if possible under NDA.

If you can drop those three items into the same Drive folder we can close out the SIG packet. Appreciate the responsiveness.

Regards,
Jacob
